newsitem.title: UK: Forth Ports to operate intermodal terminal.
newsitem.headline: Forth Ports to operate intermodal terminal.

text.p: Forth Ports Plc today said it expects to put a new intermodal terminal at Tilbury, east London, into operation this autumn.

The Scottish ports group said it had was close to agreeing terms to build the terminal on 28 acres of land and track purchased last year from the British Rail Property Board adjacent to the Port of Tilbury which it acquired in 1995.

Forth Ports chief executive Alistair Fleming told Reuters in a telephone interview: "We are very close to deciding to go ahead with building an intermodal rail facility on this land. The terminal should be ready to operate by August or September."

Fleming said Forth Ports was talking to British rail container operator Freightliner and two European freight carrier operators which he declined to name. The business would involve the movement of swap body equipment.
He said the company was planning to reinstate the rail facilities which used to serve seaborne passenger traffic for Australia and build a trailer park.
He added: "We see this as an important strategic opportunity for the future of the group."

Forth Ports also has outline planning permission for the construction of warehouse and distribution facilities on 50 acres of property at Fort Land which it owns on the other side of the proposed terminal.
The group said: "Final consent should be forthcoming shortly. The uplift in value arising from this consent will be incorporated in the 1997 balance sheet."
It added that a "prudent value of the land was taken and substantially written down" when it acquired Tilbury.
Forth Ports added it had "successfully integrated the ports of Tilbury and Dundee into the group, following their acquisition in 1995".

It reported earlier today that pre-tax profits had increased by 45 percent over the year to December 31, 1996 to 22.2 million sterling from 15.3 million. Turnover rose 79 percent to 84.7 million sterling, Forth said.

The group said it has a number of dry bulk projects in hand at Tilbury including the construction of a new animal feed shed for Agriprem, plus new pulp and paper storage facilities for Sweden's Svenska Cellulosa AB (SCA) and warehousing for fresh produce.
Forth Ports said overall cargo tonnages had increased to 53.7 million tonnes from 48.7 million tonnes in 1995.
But it said: "Piped cargo tonnage was down by over one million tonnes which reflected a disappointing year at Hound Point."
Fleming said oil cargoes fell by just under 1.4 million tonnes partly due to lower levels of oil carried through the Forties pipeline and a slightly higher offtake by the Grangemouth refinery.
He added: "The fall is not a trend and this year has got off to a good start. It is our belief that tonnages at Hound Point will remain at levels we have previously seen of around 33 million tonnes."
